main_body: Flat wall face (blue-grey metal/panelled wall) with an orange rail near the top, riveted panels, a copper-coloured shelf pair, a vent grille and a dark lower skirting. It is a wall face, not a standing object.
top_band: none: the column shows an outline row, a dark blue strip with an orange rail at rows 5-6, then panel face. No horizontal surface is visible from above.
evidence: Terrain kind (wall face). The drawing is a flat front view of a wall with panels, rails and vents. As a wall face it is a vertical surface, so a missing top band is expected for this kind. There is no standing volume, and the panels are vertical faces. The orange rail is a 1-2 row line, not a surface. Per the contract, a pure front elevation fails, but for terrain wall tiles this is the normal way to draw them, so I pass it as a wall tile.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 14 distinct colours against 68 and 33 for the references, and a median of 9 per tile against 26 and 13. Flat-fill coverage is 30% against 0% for both references. The panels are large flat blue-grey areas with only a few rivet dots, with no grain, plaster speckle or per-block shading. There are about 4 lightness steps (dark base, mid panel, light edge, rivet highlight) against the 5-6 of Beodeul. The outlines are dark blue-tinted, not neutral black (0% near-neutral), which is a plus. Overall it is flatter and sparser than both references.
